== Biography ==
James Glasgow (recorded often with spelling variations like Glasow, Glasgoue, Glasgou) was christened on '''11 May 1712''' in Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. His parents were recorded as Patrick Glasow and Helen Fairbarn<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-GMN : 16 September 2021), James Glasow, 1712. Parents: Patrick Glasow, Helen Fairbarn. Christening Date: 11 May 1712, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland.</ref>. (A birth date of 5 May 1712 is given with this christening).

He married Elizabath Tait (also spelled Elizabeth) on '''25 January 1740''' in Stitchel, Roxburghshire<ref>"Scotland Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYQ1-SPB : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow marriage to Elizabath Tait, 25 Jan 1740, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland.</ref>.

Based on available christening records, James and Elizabath had the following children primarily in Stitchel, with a later record in Swinton:
* [[Glasgow-1225|Patrick Glasgow (bef.1742-)]] (Glasgoue), christened 20 June 1742 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-5XM : 16 September 2021), James Glasgoue in entry for Patrick Glasgow, 1742. Christening Date: 20 Jun 1742, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgoue, Elizabath Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgow-1218|David Glasgow (bef.1744-)]], christened 6 June 1744 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMQ-472 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Daved Glasgou, 1744. Christening Date: 06 Jun 1744, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgow, Elizabeth Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgoue-1|James Glasgoue (abt.1746-)]], christened 27 July 1746 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-R58 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgoue in entry for James Glasgoue, 1746. Christening Date: 27 Jul 1746, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgoue, Elizabath Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgou-2|Elspeth Glasgou (abt.1748-)]], christened 27 March 1748 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMM-R73 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgou in entry for Elspeth Glasgou, 1748. Christening Date: 27 Mar 1748, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgou, Elizabath Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgow-3513|Helen Glasgow (1750-)]], christened 2 April 1750 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMM-93V : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Heling Glasgow, 1750. Christening Date: 02 Apr 1750, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgow, Elizabath Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgow-1223|William Glasgow (bef.1765-abt.1820)]], christened 4 August 1765 in Swinton, Berwickshire<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBH-LM1 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for William Glasgow, 1765. Christening Date: 04 Aug 1765, Swinton, Berwickshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgow, Elizabeth Tait.</ref>. (Note the location change and time gap).

'''Important Note on Son John:''' [[Glasgow-1606|John Glasgow]] (born circa 1738, husband of Mary Robertson) has previously been identified as a son of this James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait. However, a christening record for John naming these parents has not yet been located or cited in this profile alongside his siblings listed above. Confirmation of this parental link is required (See Research Notes).

No death information for James is currently cited.

== Research Notes ==
=== Father confidence review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1440]] is assessed at 86% (probable). The cited1712 Stichill child James names Patrick Glasow and Helen Fairbarn. Their1707 Stichill/Eccles marriages and1708–1716 children identify a specific adult household. James’s1740 Stichill marriage at about28 is a plausible local continuation. The profile’s unsupported Uphall/c5May field conflicts with the cited11May Stichill event and no source directly joins the child to Elizabeth Tait’s husband, so the complete father placement is probable rather than certain.

Complete Patrick-household to James-profile placement86%; Patrick’s own identification with the1667 Gordon child is separate. No new vital field or maternal certainty change. Underlying register uninspected.

Next useful test: Reconcile James’s1712 event with the1740 marriage and retained Uphall claim; seek residence or relatives in the marriage entry.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-GMN "Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-GMN : 16 September 2021), James Glasow, 1712. Parents: Patrick Glasow, Helen Fairbarn. Christening Date: 11 May 1712, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland.]. No new original was inspected in this review. This is an assessment of an existing attachment, not a new father.


=== Leitholm working-family review — 17 October 2026 ===

James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait are the maintained Stichill parent couple, with children indexed from the 1740s and a later Swinton comparison. Robert Glasgow-3706 of Leitholm is now selected locally as a possible son at 34%; no record yet names that relationship.

Select James Glasgow (Glasgow-1238), the father recorded with Elizabath/Elizabeth Tait at Stichill, as Robert Glasgow’s possible working father, at 34%. The couple’s maintained marriage citation is dated 25 January 1740; their David and James children are indexed in June 1744 and July 1746. Robert’s estimated 1745 birth fits that family generation and could fall between those events; it is not a dated baptism. Stichill and Eccles/Leitholm belong to the same small Borders district, and the later Swinton entry attributed to the James/Tait couple offers a further local comparison. Robert’s earlier son James supplies a modest naming clue consistent with this father; a common forename cannot establish paternity. The combination favours this existing, record-defined family over the catalogue’s distant Kirknewton candidates, whose apparent proximity came from mapping Leitholm to South Leith. No inspected record names Robert as James’s son.

This is a preferred, revisable hypothesis, with 34% subjective confidence, not a measured probability or a confident connection. Robert’s 1745 birth and 8 August 1800 death each have zero attached sources on the inspected FamilySearch tree. Neither date establishes an age or place of birth. The local 1745 estimate is retained unchanged. FamilySearch attaches John Glasgow (1720–1785, GFNP-FS8) and Agnes Spark (1722–deceased, K8CD-HCW) as parents; retain that alternative without treating a contributed tree as documentary proof. The evidential basis of that parent attachment has not yet been reviewed. Do not equate that John with the much older John Glasgow-1057, husband of Agnes Spark-330, from the matching names alone. James’s brother John Glasgow-1444, christened at Stichill in 1708, is another compatible local father-generation alternative with no presently inspected Robert link. An unrecorded local father or another kinship degree remains possible. The Swinton/1740 couple continuity and Robert’s own early life need testing. Elizabeth Tait is not selected as Robert’s mother: her marriage and maternity of other children do not identify his mother. Robert is not merged with an earlier child, and James’s existing older ancestry retains its own uncertainty.

The Edinburgh Castle clergy comparison was withdrawn on 6 October: the Fasti identification belongs to James Glasgow-1140. The generic comparison re-added on 17 October is superseded; it supplies no evidence for this family.

Inspect Robert’s 1779 marriage and children’s original Eccles entries for residence, occupation and witnesses, then check Leitholm feu/tenancy and joiner apprenticeship records for a named father or master. Test the contributed John/Agnes Spark account against actual records before identifying it with any local person. Recheck the 1765 Swinton household independently. James Glasgow-1222 (1777 Kelso, attributed to David Glasgow and Janet Hood) is a nearby child-name comparison for the 1779 James, not a selected identity; retain both record accounts unless a record resolves the different parents.

* '''Confirming Son John:''' The primary research goal is to confirm if [[Glasgow-1606|John Glasgow]] (b. c1738) is indeed the son of this James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait. A birth/christening record for John, ideally dated around 1738-1741 (before Patrick) in Stitchel or nearby, naming James and Elizabath/Elizabeth as parents, is needed. Alternatively, other documents like wills or land records might establish the connection. Without this, the link between John (b.c1738) and this James (b.1712) remains unproven.
* '''Spelling Variations:''' Note the variations in spelling for the surname (Glasgow, Glasow, Glasgoue, Glasgou) and Elizabeth's first name (Elizabath) in the records. Consistent searching across variations is recommended.
* '''Birth Date:''' The exact birth date of May 5, 1712 needs verification, as the cited record confirms the May 11, 1712 christening. Checking the original parish register image may clarify if the birth date was recorded.
* '''Gap in Children & Relocation:''' There is a 15-year gap between the christening of Heling (1750 in Stitchel) and William (1765 in Swinton, Berwickshire). This suggests other children might be missing, or the family relocated during this period. The reason for the move from Roxburghshire to Berwickshire is unknown. Research in Swinton records around 1765 might provide further clues.
* '''Death Records:''' Death or burial records for James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait are needed. They might be found in Stitchel, Swinton, or potentially elsewhere depending on later movements.

=== Possible James Glasgow, Edinburgh Castle clergy, 1737–1738 ===
James Glasgow, styled Clerk, is appointed chaplain to the garrison of Edinburgh Castle by a royal commission reported read in the presbytery.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1142270617/ The Daily Gazetteer, 1737-11-03, p.1].</ref>

James Glasgow, probationer, is reported ordained minister of the Castle in an Edinburgh-datelined notice.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1142271259/ The Daily Gazetteer, 1738-02-23, p.1].</ref>

The 1737 commission and 1738 ordination appear to concern the same Castle officeholder; the newspaper notices give no parents.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1238]]. Adult in 1737–1738; recorded recorded lifespan extends beyond the events. No clergy, Edinburgh Castle, or identifying location evidence in the comparison summary.
